title: The western Loire
subtitle: Muscadet, Anjou and Saumur
objectives: Describe Anjou's whites and sweet wines

steps.title: Muscadet
steps.body: In the Pays Nantais, Muscadet is made from Melon de Bourgogne: light, crisp and saline. Muscadet Sèvre et Maine is the main appellation. Sur lie wines rest on their lees until bottling, gaining texture and a slight spritz. Since 2011, crus communaux, like Clisson and Gorges, show longer-aged, serious Muscadet.

steps.title: Anjou
steps.body: Anjou makes Chenin Blanc in every style. Savennières, on schist, gives dry, powerful, long-lived whites. The Layon valley, with autumn mists, gives sweet botrytised wines: Coteaux du Layon, Bonnezeaux and Quarts de Chaume, the Loire's first Grand Cru, in 2011. Anjou also makes rosés like Rosé d'Anjou and Cabernet d'Anjou.

steps.prompt: Which Loire appellation became the first Grand Cru, in 2011?
steps.explanation: Quarts de Chaume makes sweet, botrytised Chenin.

steps.title: Saumur
steps.body: Saumur, with tuffeau soils and cellars, makes Saumur Brut, a traditional method sparkling wine, mainly from Chenin Blanc, and Saumur-Champigny, a fresh, fruity Cabernet Franc red. Many sparkling houses, like Bouvet-Ladubay and Gratien & Meyer, are based there, ageing wine in tuffeau caves.

steps.explanation: Sancerre is in the Central Vineyards.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Muscadet is crisp Melon, often sur lie
Anjou makes dry Savennières and sweet Layon Chenin
Saumur makes sparkling wine and Cabernet Franc reds
